facts.text: Northville is a city divided almost equally between Oakland County to the north and Wayne County to the south, with Eight Mile Road serving as the county line.
The City of Northville is independent of Northville Township, which borders it to the south.
Northville grew through the Victorian era, and many homes around downtown are in the Queen Anne style.
The Northville Historic District, listed on the National Register of Historic Places in 1972, is primarily residential, and the majority of it is Gothic Revival houses built between 1860 and 1880.
The historic district includes commercial buildings on East Main Street such as the Masonic Hall at 106 E. Main, whose first story was built in 1880, and the Freydl Stores, built in 1875.
Mill Race Village on Griswold opened in 1972 on the site of John Miller's gristmill and gathers historic buildings such as the Yerkes House and the Cady Inn.
Downtown Northville's holiday season opens with the annual Holiday Lighted Parade, followed by the official tree lighting in Town Square.
Maybury State Park, a 1,000-acre park at 49601 Eight Mile Road with a Northville address, offers rolling hills, open meadows and trails on the former site of the Maybury Sanatorium.

christmas-light-installation.title: Christmas Light Installation in Northville, MI
christmas-light-installation.meta_description: Northville Christmas light installation built around steep Gothic Revival gables and Queen Anne porches, with in-season service and takedown included.
christmas-light-installation.h1: Christmas Light Installation in Northville, MI
christmas-light-installation.hero_sub: Christmas lights that follow the gables, porches and trim of older homes, hung by bucket-truck crews and looked after until it all comes down after the holidays.
christmas-light-installation.local_paragraph: Most of the Northville Historic District is Gothic Revival houses built between 1860 and 1880, and many homes around downtown are Queen Anne. Both styles are hard on a lazy lighting job. Gothic Revival houses are known for steep, pointed gables and decorative trim along the eaves, and a steep gable shows every sag. Queen Anne homes add towers, bays and deep porches, which means more corners and more places for a line to wander. We plan each run against the architecture, reach the peaks from a bucket truck when the lot has room, and let porch columns and railings carry part of the display. The result looks deliberate from the street and from down the block.
considerations: A steep gable shows every gap and sag. We measure each pitch, hang the run from the bucket wherever the truck can reach, and look at the line from the street before moving on to the next one.
Frame the detail, do not bury it

On a house with carved trim or ornate porch work, the lights should frame the craftsmanship. A single warm white outline and lit porch columns can do more than heavy color, and we will talk through both looks during the estimate.

During the estimate we check where a bucket truck can park, what is overhead and how close the drive is to the house. Installation day then starts with a plan instead of guesswork, and the crew knows the property before it arrives.
faq: Do you serve both the City of Northville and Northville Township?

Yes. The city, on both sides of Eight Mile Road, and Northville Township to the south are within our Southeast Michigan service area. Reach us at (248) 756-8915, or send your address through the form, to book a free estimate.
Will lights suit a Gothic Revival or Queen Anne house?

They can look superb when the plan follows the architecture. We trace the main gables, pick out porch details and keep lights off anything too delicate to clip. The estimate shows which lines get lit, so nothing about install day is a surprise.
When should I book so the house is lit for the holidays?

Home installs commonly fall between October and early December. If you want the house lit by the time downtown holds its Holiday Lighted Parade and Town Square tree lighting, request early for the widest choice of dates.

commercial-holiday-lighting.title: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Northville, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.meta_description: Holiday lighting for historic storefronts and facades in downtown Northville, plus offices and HOA entrances. Free walkthrough and written estimate.
commercial-holiday-lighting.h1: Commercial Holiday Lighting in Northville, MI
commercial-holiday-lighting.hero_sub: Cornice outlines, window framing and tree wraps for historic storefronts, offices and multi-tenant buildings downtown, plus entrance displays for associations nearby.
commercial-holiday-lighting.local_paragraph: Downtown Northville opens its holiday season with the Holiday Lighted Parade and the official tree lighting in Town Square. Its historic district reaches East Main Street, where the Freydl Stores date to 1875 and the Masonic Hall's first story went up in 1880. Commercial buildings of that age tend to have cornices, tall upper windows and detailed storefronts, and those are the lines worth lighting. Outline the cornice, frame the upper windows, wrap the tree by the door, and the building reads as part of the season. Attachment is planned around older trim and storefront details. Bucket-truck crews do the high work, and in-season service covers the display until removal once the season ends.
considerations: A light touch on older fronts

Some of East Main Street's commercial buildings date to the 1870s and 1880s. At the walkthrough we look at how the cornice, window trim and storefront are put together before choosing where anything attaches, and we plan a layout that comes down cleanly after the season.

The Holiday Lighted Parade and the Town Square tree lighting set the tone downtown. If you want the building lit for the parade, say so at the walkthrough and we will plan the schedule backward from it.
One look for a whole block

Neighboring businesses and property managers sometimes want matching outlines across several storefronts. We can plan and estimate the buildings together, so the block reads as one display and each owner knows their share.
faq: Can you light a historic storefront downtown?

Yes. We light storefronts, offices and multi-tenant buildings across our service area, which includes downtown Northville. A free walkthrough looks at the facade, the power and where a lift can safely work, and the estimate spells out design, installation, service and removal.
Can you light an HOA entrance in Northville Township?

Yes. For subdivisions in Northville Township, we plan the display around the entrance monument, the sign and the plantings that frame the turn in. Boards receive a written estimate to discuss and approve, and in-season service covers the entrance until removal.
What happens if part of the display goes dark?

Call us and we will schedule a service visit. In-season service is part of our commercial work, and the estimate spells out how it works for your building, so you know what to expect before the season starts.

permanent-lighting.title: Permanent Lighting in Northville, MI
permanent-lighting.meta_description: Permanent roofline lighting for Northville homes, planned around Victorian gables and corners. App-controlled scenes for every season.
permanent-lighting.hero_sub: A discreet track under the eaves and lights you run from your phone, all year. Planned around every gable, bay and corner of your roofline.
permanent-lighting.local_paragraph: Permanent lighting is roofline lighting that stays up year-round. A low-profile track sits under the eaves, and the lights inside it answer to an app on your phone. In Northville, the interesting question is the roofline itself. A Queen Anne house can turn many corners between the porch and the peak, and a Gothic Revival home climbs to steep, pointed gables. We measure every angle, plan where each run starts and ends, and work out where the power comes from. Once it is in, the app does the rest: a Christmas scene in December, school colors for homecoming, a soft outline on a timer every evening.
considerations: Bays, towers and cross gables add up to a lot of angles. We measure each one and design the runs so the outline looks continuous from the street, even where the roof changes direction several times.

Before you commit to anything permanent on a house in the Northville Historic District, ask the city whether exterior changes at your address need review. Bring our written estimate to that conversation: it shows the route of the track and how it mounts, so the question can be answered on specifics.

Because the track tucks under the eaves, it stays discreet in daylight. At the estimate we look at your trim color and talk through how the installed track will sit against it, so the house looks right at noon as well as at night.
faq: Is a Queen Anne roofline too complicated for permanent lighting?

Not usually. It takes more measuring and more planning at the corners, but complex rooflines are where a continuous outline looks most striking. If a section would not look right, we will say so and suggest leaving it dark.
What can I do with the app?
Choose colors and scenes, then schedule when the lights turn on and off. Save a Christmas scene, a Halloween scene and an everyday warm white setting, and switch between them with a tap.
What happens at a permanent lighting estimate?

A visit to measure the roofline, a count of runs and corners, a check of where power is available, and a written estimate for the layout, installation and app setup. It is free for homes in the city and in Northville Township.
